questions.question: Which mirror is used by doctors to examine the eyes, ears, nose, and throat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Concave mirror**.

__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• The mirror which has a spherical reflecting surface is called a spherical mirror.

There are two types of spherical mirror:

Convex mirror:

 
• The spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is away from the center of curvature is called a convex mirror.
 
• It always from a virtual image of any object.

Concave mirror:

 
• The mirror whose reflecting surface is inward is called a concave mirror.
 
• It can form both real as well as a virtual image of any object.

 And for concave mirror image formed when the object is placed at different locations are

if an object is placed beyond the center of curvature then the image will be real, inverted, and diminish

 
• if an object is placed at the center of curvature then the image will be real, inverted and of the same size
 
• if an object is placed at the principal focus image formed in this case will be highly enlarged, real and inverted.
 
• if an object is placed between the principal focus and pole of the mirror then the image will be virtual, erect, and magnified
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0a7b08f7def9b7610813baabc7d001e3e602d85e09c407eaf215cab43a85d09.png] 

Explanation:__

__
 
• When the object is between the center of curvature and focus or between the focus and pole of a concave mirror, the image formed is virtual, erect, and magnified.
 
• Therefore, doctors use concave mirrors__ to examine the eyes, ears, nose, and throat from a close range as the image formed is enlarged and provides a better view to the doctor.

questions.question: Which force is responsible for deflecting winds towards the right and left in northern and southern Hemisphere respectively?

__
 
• **Coriolis force:-**

 
 
• It​ is responsible for **deflecting winds** towards the** right and left** in the northern and southern hemispheres respectively.
 
• This force is a result of the** rotation of the Earth** and the** inertia of the moving air masses.**
 
• The Coriolis force is** strongest at the poles **and **weakest at the equator.**
 
• This force also affects **ocean currents** and the movement of objects such as **airplanes and missiles.**

• This force is caused by the **interaction of charged particles **with **Earth's magnetic field.**
 
• It can affect the behavior of **charged particles** in the atmosphere, but it does not have a significant impact on wind deflection.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational force:**
 
 
• This force is responsible for** keeping objects on Earth's surface** and is not directly related to wind deflection.
 
 
 
• **Frictional force:**
 
 
• This force is caused by the interaction of air with the Earth's surface and can affect **wind speed and direction**, but it is not responsible for wind deflection.

questions.question: The potential difference, V, across the ends of a given metallic wire in an electric circuit is directly proportional to the current flowing through it, provided its temperature remains the same. This is called ______ law.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Ohm's**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The relationship between current, voltage, and resistance is described by Ohm's law. This law is given by George Simon Ohm in 1828

Ohm’s law:__

__
 
• Ohm’s law states that at a constant temperature, the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• Voltage = Current × Resistance
 
 
• V = I × R
 
• V = voltage, I = current and R = resistance
 
 
 
• The SI unit of resistance is ohms and is denoted by Ω.
 
• It helps to calculate the power, efficiency, current, voltage, and resistance of an element of an electrical circuit.
 
• If an element follows ohm’s law, then the element is known as a linear element.
 
• Ex: Resistor

Limitation of ohm's Law:__

__
 
• Ohm’s law is applicable for conductors only.
 
• Ohm’s law does not apply to unilateral networks. Unilateral networks allow the current to flow in one direction. Such types of networks consist of elements like a diode, transistor, etc.
 
• Ohm’s law is also not applicable to non - linear elements.
 
• Non-linear elements are those which do not have current exactly proportional to the applied voltage that means the resistance value of those elements changes for different values of voltage and current. An example of a non-linear element is a thyristor.
 
• Ohm’s law is also not applicable to vacuum tubes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Boyle’s Law**

 
• ​Boyle's law is a gas law that states that a gas's pressure and volume are inversely proportional.
 
• It states that at a constant temperature, the pressure exerted by a gas is inversely proportional to the volume occupied by it.
 
• According to the Boyle's Law:
 
 
• P1V1 = P2V2
 
 
• Where P1 = Initial Pressure

 P2 = Final Pressure

 V1 = Initial Volume 

 V2 = Final Volume

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/883ca4a9c62fe7d942ab5573518c8cee4603dd50fc0953b220b928a0f514f177.png] 
 
 
 
 

The five main gas laws in chemistry are Boyle's Law, Charle's Law, Gay Lussac's Law, Avogadro's Law, and Ideal Gas Law.

 
• Charle's law states that the volume of an ideal gas is directly proportional to the absolute temperature at constant pressure.
 
• Gay-Lussac's law states that the pressure of a given mass of gas varies directly with the absolute temperature of the gas when the volume is kept constant.
 
• Avogadro's law or Avogadro-Ampère's hypothesis is an experimental gas law relating the volume of a gas to the amount of substance of gas present.
 
• The ideal gas law states that the product of the pressure and the volume of one gram molecule of an ideal gas is equal to the product of the absolute temperature of the gas and the universal gas constant.

__
 
• **The ampere** often shortened to** 'amp'** is the **SI base unit of electric current.**
 
• The ampere (symbol: A) is the SI base unit of electric current **equal to one coulomb per second.**
 
• **One ampere is equal to 6.241509074×1018 electrons **worth of charge moving past a point in a second.
 
• It is named after the **French mathematician and physicist Andre Marie Ampere** considered** the father of electromagnetism **along with** Danish physicist Hans Christian Orsted.**

• It is named after the Italian physicist Alessandro Volta.
 
• **One volt is defined as the electric potential between two points of a conducting wire when an electric current of one ampere dissipates one watt of power between those points.**
 
• Equivalently, it is the potential difference between two points that will impart one joule of energy per coulomb of charge that passes through it.
 
• It can be** expressed in terms of SI base units (m, kg, s, and A).**

__

• It is named after the **Belfast-born and University of Glasgow-based engineer and physicist William Thomson, 1st Baron Kelvin.**
 
• The Kelvin scale is an absolute thermodynamic temperature scale, meaning it uses absolute zero as its null point.
 
• The Kelvin scale was developed by shifting the starting point of the much older Celsius scale down from the melting point of water to absolute zero.

• The candela has replaced the standard candle or lamp as a unit of luminous intensity in calculations involving artificial lighting and is sometimes called the “**new candle**".

questions.question: Which of the following is measured in the unit called Gauss?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetic induction**__.

__
 
• **Gauss **is the **SI unit** of **Magnetic induction**.

 
 
• The **gauss **(**G)** is used for the **measurement **of **magnetic induction**, also known as **magnetic flux density**.
 
• In the **CGS system **or the** centimetre gram second system **of various physical units, **gauss **is the unit of **magnetic induction**.
 
• Generally, an **electromotive force **will be **induced **by the **application **of **magnetic flux density**.
 
• The **unit **was **named **after a **German scientist **by the name of **Carl Friedrich Gauss**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnetic induction **was discovered by **Michael Faraday **in **1831**.

 
 
• **Magnetic induction**, also called **electromagnetic induction **refers to the **production **of **voltage **(or EMF) across an **electrical conductor **placed **inside **a **varying magnetic field**.
 
• According to **Faraday’s law**, for a** closed circuit**, the **induced electromotive force** is **equal **to the **rate of change of the magnetic flux** **enclosed **by the **circuit**.
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction** is a **current produced **because of **voltage production **(electromotive force) due to a **changing magnetic **field.
 
• This **either **happens when a **conductor **is **placed **in a **moving magnetic field **(when using an AC power source) or when a **conductor **is **constantly moving **in a **stationary magnetic field**.
